The gap is marked resolved, the two source-grounded entries now cite the receipt, and a fact records the executed consequence.

investigations.discriminator: No conjecture in this account is left undecided. What would extend or bound it is behaviour outside the exercised windows and stores: a partition that leaves the rewritten and the replaced configurations with separate quorums and leadership, a disk-backed commit-tracking store, crash and restart timing, and repeated or longer runs. Those are recorded as limitations rather than as open questions.

knowledge.statement: A leader accepts a client membership change as soon as its own latest configuration is committed and it has committed an entry in its term (configurationChangeChIfStable), then computes the new configuration with nextConfiguration from configurations.latest and the request, appends it, immediately installs it as the latest configuration and rebuilds the leader's commitment from it; the request's prevIndex, when nonzero, is the only guard against acting on a different configuration than the caller expected.
knowledge.conditions: The node is leader and its configurations.latest is the one reconstructed at startup rather than the configuration recorded in its log; a client calls AddVoter, AddNonvoter, DemoteVoter or RemoveServer with prevIndex 0 (the package's AddPeer and RemovePeer helpers use 0, and callers may too); the gate does not consult the log's own configuration entry.

knowledge.statement: Because the appended configuration entry is immediately the leader's latest configuration and the leader's commitment is rebuilt from it, the quorum that commits a membership change is the reconstructed one, not the committed configuration's quorum: with a reconstruction that has fewer voters than the committed configuration, a change can be committed with support that is not a majority of the configuration being replaced and can include a peer that is not in it, and the peers of the committed configuration that the reconstruction no longer counts as voters are not asked for support at all.
knowledge.conditions: A node whose reconstruction is smaller than the committed configuration leads; a client membership change is issued to that leader with prevIndex 0; the reconstruction keeps the other peers as members so replication can still reach them. Exercised in receipt 2caa49e2796e4a19884ddafd38610f91: the change committed with the leader and a fresh instance as the only voters of the new configuration, while the configuration entry in the leader's own log named three voters.
knowledge.changed_premise: The earlier revision stated the consequence from source reasoning and recorded that no client membership change had been issued in this run. The channel is now exercised, so the conditions cite the receipt instead of the absence of an execution; the statement is unchanged.

knowledge.statement: In the retained client-change execution the committed membership was rewritten without the replaced configuration's majority: the leader had reconstructed one voter against the three voters recorded at index 110 in its own log, its client AddVoter with prevIndex 0 completed (change_committed true), and its configuration afterwards had two voters — itself and the fresh instance, which was not part of the replaced configuration — with the two peers that had held votes there carried as nonvoters. Both of those peers, restarted with the flag disabled, adopted the rewritten configuration (demoted_peers_adopted 2) and held no vote in it (demoted_peers_with_vote 0), while with the flag disabled the same node could not be leader with the others down, the change failed with "node is not the leader" and both peers kept their votes.
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter committed configuration recorded at log index 110 while the restarted leader's snapshot metadata carries a single-voter configuration; only the leader and one fresh empty instance run while the change is issued, and the fresh instance is connected to the leader in both directions; the two peers of the committed configuration are restarted afterwards with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled. The change is the package's own AddVoter with prevIndex 0; no partition, no concurrent client change and no nonzero prevIndex case is exercised.

The current account therefore stands, each result under its own receipt: NewRaft's configuration scan starts above max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied) and restoreFromCommittedLogs advances lastApplied to the tracked commit index first, so a committed configuration entry inside that prefix is never re-derived [scan_start, restore_lastapplied, cfg_entry]; the reconstruction differs from the node's own log in both directions across five exercised shapes; and that context then produces bounded non-progress, leadership and commits resting on a minority, a client-acknowledged commit either resting on one copy or discarded from every store, a vote granted and durably recorded for a peer without a vote, leadership acquired by a peer without a vote, and now a client membership change that replaced the committed configuration with support that was not its majority and demoted its voters [change_gate, append_config_change, next_configuration, commitment_set_config]. What remains outside is stated below as limitations; the earlier question-level supplement that recorded this channel as unexercised is superseded by this receipt.

9a41509dc6bc4af0b0995cf14bf9918c-gap-1.explanation: Yes, and the demoted peers adopt it. Executed in receipt 2caa49e2796e4a19884ddafd38610f91: with the reconstruction holding one voter, a client AddVoter with prevIndex 0 completed and the resulting configuration had two voters including a member outside the replaced configuration, so the change committed with support that was not a majority of the configuration it replaced and never asked its two voter peers for support; both of them, restarted afterwards, adopted the rewritten configuration and hold no vote in it. The control with the flag disabled could not lead and made no change.

counterevidence: The feature's documented purpose is replaying known-committed logs into the FSM; nothing in the sources makes skipping committed configuration entries a required behaviour, and the existing TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs asserts only applied index, tracked commit index and log indices, so it neither exercises nor contradicts the configuration reconstruction.

Competing explanation that the flag's committed-log replay itself, rather than the skipped configuration entry, produces these effects: excluded wherever tested, by the within-flag case whose configuration entry lies above the replayed prefix and by the flag-disabled controls in every receipt, which hold the published configuration and refuse the same requests, decisions and changes.

The client-change channel needs prevIndex 0 and the peers of the committed configuration to be unreachable while the change is issued: a caller passing the committed configuration's index is rejected with "configuration changed since", and a reachable peer holding a vote would have to acknowledge the entry for it to commit under the committed quorum. The consequence therefore holds under stated conditions rather than unconditionally.

In every case the returning or answering peers were rebuilt with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled unless the case was about their own divergence, and the membership ladders were built from demote/promote or remove; what is exercised is one divergent node's context in a cluster of otherwise correct nodes.
limitations: Single process with in-memory transports and in-memory commit-tracking stores, no crash injection, no disk-backed store and no network fault model.

Single-shot windows (200-1500 ms depending on the case, 3000 ms for leadership, 1000-1500 ms for commits) and one or two restarted instances per case; no rate, repetition or long-run stability claim follows.

The rewritten-membership consequence is exercised without a partition, so no claim is made about leadership among the rewritten and replaced configurations running at the same time, which is the natural next boundary to test.

The earlier delivered-request vote case carries a synthesized campaign and term claim; the self-produced campaign receipt supersedes it, and pre-vote-only campaigns were not exercised in isolation. The LogCache entries record a separate startup-plumbing gap rather than a consensus consequence.
